*Interrogator note prepared for the investment committee. Currency is Swiss francs (CHF) throughout; Kuehne + Nagel is listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange. Transcripts reviewed span the nine-month 2024 call (2024-10-23) through the first-quarter 2026 call (2026-04-24). Live share price used: 210.60 CHF (July 17, 2026), trading near its 52-week high of 213.70 CHF.*

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

Kuehne + Nagel is the world's largest sea- and air-freight forwarder — the "middleman" that books space on other people's ships and planes and manages the paperwork, rather than owning the vessels itself (an "asset-light" model). Across these five calls the story travels a full cycle: from post-boom hangover, into a painful margin squeeze, and out the other side into an early, self-help-driven stabilization.

- **Late 2024 (the hangover):** Management framed 2024 as a recovery "in line with expectations" but repeatedly walked back its own mid-year optimism. The CEO conceded "diminished prospects for this year['s] peak season relative to our views at mid-year," blaming customers front-loading cargo ahead of the US election and Red Sea disruption. The emphasis was on cost control and "right-sizing" the workforce after the 2021–2022 freight super-cycle collapsed.
- **Q1 2025 (false dawn):** The tone brightened — "market share up, profits up," 8% gross-profit growth, a large US drayage acquisition (IMC) folded in. Management leaned into a flexible, "asset-light" model amid tariff volatility.
- **Late 2025 (the squeeze):** The narrative deteriorated sharply. "Overcapacity and softer demand" crushed yields; nine-month group operating profit (EBIT) fell 13% excluding currency. Sea and air conversion (the share of gross profit that drops to operating profit) collapsed, Sea Logistics conversion falling to 24% in the third quarter from 35% a year earlier. Management pivoted hard to defense, announcing a cost-reduction program of "at least CHF 200 million."
- **FY 2025 → Q1 2026 (the turn):** The new story is stabilization plus self-help. Yields "stabilized" for two straight quarters, the cost program is "running ahead of plan," Road Logistics inflected (EBIT +42% year-over-year in Q1 2026), and Contract Logistics printed record after record. A newly introduced fourth pillar — artificial intelligence, with a freshly minted Chief AI and Innovation Officer — became the forward growth hook.

Growth drivers quietly **dropped:** the 2021–2022 freight-rate windfall (never to return), and the Apex e-commerce air-freight engine (hurt badly by the US ending the "de minimis" duty exemption that powered cheap cross-border parcels). Drivers **introduced:** hyperscaler/semiconductor air freight ("about half of Q3 2025 air volume growth"), customs-clearance consulting as tariffs proliferate, SME (small and mid-sized enterprise) share gains at 1.6–1.8x the average gross profit, and AI-driven productivity.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The hard numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "We reinforced our #1 position in sea and air freight" (FY2025) | ROIC ~25%, ROE ~50% — genuinely best-in-class for a forwarder | **Matches.** The quality is real. |
| "Market share up, profits up" (Q1 2025) | Revenue -1.3% year-over-year; 3-year revenue decline of ~15% annualized; EPS -25% year-over-year | **Diverges.** Share may be rising, but earnings power fell hard — 2025 EPS of 7.42 is a third of the 22.03 printed in 2022. |
| Yields have "stabilized" (FY2025, Q1 2026) | Sea conversion 25% in Q1 2026 vs 35% a year earlier; group EBIT still -17% year-over-year in Q1 2026 | **Partly.** Sequential stabilization is real; the year-over-year level is still deeply depressed. |
| Cost program "running ahead of plan," CHF 200M savings | Q1 2026 recurring EBIT of 308M "exceeded guidance"; ~half of upside attributed to cost phasing | **Matches so far.** Early evidence supports it — full run-rate only by year-end 2026. |
| Free cash flow conversion improving | Q4 2025 conversion 147%, full-year 86%; but Q1 2026 underlying conversion only 40% and working-capital intensity rose to 6% (above the 4.5–5.5% target) | **Mixed.** The heralded cash story is seasonally lumpy and leaned on a one-time real-estate sale-and-leaseback (a CHF 35M gain) in Q1 2026. |

The through-line: the narrative is **richer than the trajectory justifies on earnings** (EPS has fallen for three straight years) but **honest about the cycle** — management has not tried to hide the yield collapse.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Rating: **turning up from a defensive trough.**

- **2024-10-23 (defensive):** apologetic and hedged — "diminished prospects," "muted peak season," repeated downgrades of mid-year hopes.
- **2025-04-24 (briefly offensive):** "market share up, profits up," confidence in the "flexible asset-light business model."
- **2025-10-23 (most defensive):** "overcapacity puts pressure on yields," an emergency cost program announced, EBIT guidance cut to ">CHF 1.3 billion."
- **2026-03-03 / 2026-04-24 (measured optimism returns):** "recurring EBIT exceeded our guidance," "running ahead of plan," a guidance raise to the lower end. Language shifts back toward offense (AI, hyperscalers, new contracts "in the implementation phase") while staying grounded.

The clear arc is from offense (2024 growth) to deep defense (2025 cost-cutting) and back to cautious offense (2026 self-help plus early cyclical stabilization).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Reliability: **Medium-to-High, improving.** The record is two-sided. Through 2024–2025 management serially over-promised on peak seasons and had to cut 2025 EBIT guidance mid-year — consistent with the mediocre 43% earnings-beat rate (3 of 7 quarters) in our data. But the most recent cut was set at a level they then **beat** (Q1 2026 recurring EBIT of 308M above their own guide), and the CHF 200M cost program is tracking ahead of schedule. The pattern is a management that reset expectations low enough after the 2025 shock that it can now clear the bar — credible, but the credibility is newly re-earned, not long-standing.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

- **Capital return / buyback vs dividend (recurring):** Morgan Stanley's Cedar Ekblom pressed in late 2025 on switching from dividends to buybacks "considering where shares are." Management deflected — the Supervisory Board's "preference is on the side of dividends." This matters: it forecloses the buyback that a deep-value re-rating would normally need.
- **Apex put option (recurring, 2024→2025):** analysts (DB's Andy Chu) probed Partners Group's 24.9% Apex stake for a year; management was non-committal ("I have no visibility what is in the thinking of Partners Group") until it was forced — Partners Group **exercised its put** in late 2025, obliging Kuehne + Nagel to buy the stake for ~CHF 886M in cash, funded by bank loans.
- **Yield direction (recurring):** analysts repeatedly pushed on whether yields had bottomed; management's mid-2024 CHF 90/100kg air-yield target was quietly abandoned, and the 2025 yield collapse proved the bears right.
- **Unaddressed worry:** the durability of hyperscaler air volumes and whether AI is a genuine margin lever or a defensive necessity as digital forwarders and automation compress the forwarder's value-add.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🔴 EPS has fallen three consecutive years (22.03 → 12.02 → 9.95 → 7.42) — the base earnings power is a fraction of the 2022 peak (2025-03-03 data).
🔴 The Apex put forced a ~CHF 886M debt-funded cash outflow (2025-10-23), raising leverage into a soft market.
🔴 Working-capital intensity climbed to 6%, above the 4.5–5.5% target corridor, pressuring cash (2026-04-24).
🔴 A one-time CHF 35M real-estate gain flattered Q1 2026 recurring optics (2026-04-24).
🟢 Contract Logistics is a genuine bright spot — record EBIT, ~25% return on capital employed, healthcare and hyperscaler-driven (2026-03-03).
🟢 Yields stabilized for two straight quarters and the cost program is ahead of plan (2026-04-24).
🟢 Road Logistics inflected positively (+42% EBIT year-over-year in Q1 2026) after two weak years.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

- **Terminology shift:** "complexity into value" became the mantra — reframing tariff chaos and supply-chain disruption as a revenue opportunity (customs consulting). It is a tell that the core forwarding yield is under structural pressure and management is hunting adjacent, higher-value services.
- **New voice:** the debut of a Chief AI and Innovation Officer (2026-03-03) signals both offense (a claimed proprietary-platform edge) and defense (AI could erode the SME digital-forwarding moat that peers like Flexport target).
- **Capital allocation:** the flat refusal to buy back stock even near lows, combined with the founder-controlled register (Kühne Holding owns roughly half the shares), means the company will not self-help its own valuation and cannot be pushed by an activist.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: **PIVOTING** — a cyclical trough with an early, self-help-led turn, not a structural decline.

The single most important thing to weigh before sizing: **this is a high-quality, credibly-run market leader — but it is trading near a 52-week high, above the analyst consensus target, at roughly 28–30x trough earnings, with no forcing function to unlock value.** The founder controls the register (no activist is possible), the board prefers dividends to buybacks (no self-help re-rating), and the one hard corporate event — the Apex put — has already fired. You are being asked to pay a full-recovery price for a recovery that is only just beginning and is already visible to everyone.

**Economic moat:** scale-cost plus network, real but **NARROW**. Kuehne + Nagel earns genuinely superior returns (ROIC ~25%) from its #1 scale, but forwarding is a fragmented, competitive industry (DSV — now digesting DB Schenker — DHL, Expeditors, C.H. Robinson, Sinotrans). Pricing power is limited: the 2025 yield collapse, where Sea conversion fell from 35% to 24% as capacity flooded in, shows the company is largely a price-taker on freight rates. **Moat trend: STABLE** — returns are cyclically compressed, not structurally eroding; ROIC of ~25% remains excellent and yields have stabilized.

**Secular threat: manageable, not terminal.** Digital freight forwarders and AI could compress the value-add of matching shippers to capacity, and the loss of the US "de minimis" exemption structurally dented the Apex e-commerce air engine. But global-trade complexity (tariffs, customs, rerouting) is, if anything, rising — which increases what a scaled forwarder can charge for orchestration. Kuehne + Nagel is investing to lead the AI transition rather than be displaced by it. The cheapness signal our screener flagged is not a fear-print on a melting franchise; it is simply mislabeled — the stock is fully priced, not distressed.

Kuehne + Nagel is the world's largest sea- and air-freight forwarder — the "middleman" that books space on other people's ships and planes and manages the paperwork, rather than owning the vessels itself (an "asset-light" model). - **Late 2024 (the hangover):** Management framed 2024 as a recovery "in line with expectations" but repeatedly walked back its own mid-year optimism. The CEO conceded "diminished prospects for this year['s] peak season relative to our views at mid-year," blaming customers front-loading cargo ahead of the US election and Red Sea disruption. The emphasis was on cost control and "right-sizing" the workforce after the 2021–2022 freight super-cycle collapsed.
- **Q1 2025 (false dawn):** The tone brightened — "market share up, profits up," 8% gross-profit growth, a large US drayage acquisition (IMC) folded in. Management leaned into a flexible, "asset-light" model amid tariff volatility.
